content.text: The redline validated. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: (e) Access to Receivable Files. The Custodian will give the Servicer access to the Receivable Files and, on request of the Servicer, the Custodian will promptly release any document in the Receivable Files to the Servicer for purposes of servicing the Receivables.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind. A full-text search for "insurance" returns only unrelated references (insurance premiums billed to Obligor accounts at p0095 and FDIC deposit insurance at p0903), and Articles III, VI and X contain no coverage requirement, fidelity bond or errors-and-omissions provision. Meanwhile, Cellco is the counterparty performing services that squarely engage this rule: under Section 3.10 it acts as Custodian and "will hold and maintain in custody" the Receivable Files (p0138), maintains them and the receivables systems on which they are electronically stored (p0141, p0145), and controls access subject to its "confidentiality, privacy and data protection policies" (p0146). The Receivable Files comprise Obligor records, and the Agreement itself recognises Personally Identifiable Information as a category requiring redaction (p0446, p0884). Exhibit A ("Custodian's Security Requirements") is not reproduced in this form (sec-p1043 contains no substantive text), so no coverage requirement sits there either. That places the document in walk-away territory under this rule — no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data — so neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met. Redline inserts a new Section 10.14 in Article X Miscellaneous, per the rule's redline guidance, at the preferred level (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with terminology conformed to this Agreement (Receivable Files, Personally Identifiable Information, Obligors, applicable Law) and applied to Cellco in all three of its capacities. Noting for context: severity is low and insurance covenants are atypical in a securitization transfer and servicing agreement, where Cellco's indemnity under Section 6.3 provides some overlapping (though uncollateralised and gross-negligence-limited) protection; the fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment if the full programme is resisted.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 10.14 (Insurance) in Article X requiring Cellco, as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian, to carry CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation coverage and to provide certificates on request.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Cellco holds the Receivable Files and Obligor personally identifiable information as Servicer and Custodian, but the Agreement contains no insurance covenant, so we have added our standard coverage requirement (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). If the full programme is an issue, we can fall back to E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M.

ops.text: Section 10.14 Insurance. Cellco, in each of its capacities as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian, will maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000; (c) cyber liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000 covering its handling of the Receivable Files and any Personally Identifiable Information of the Obligors; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Cellco will provide certificates of insurance to the Issuer and the Depositor on request.
